units.title: Introduction to Industrial Engineering.
topics: 1.1. Industrial engineering-definition, objectives and techniques.
1.2. Scope, importance and applications of industrial engineering.
1.3. Methodology and approach of Industrial engineering.
1.4. Productivity – concept, definition, importance and ways to enhance it, numeric examples.
1.5. Introduction to work study.
1.6. Introduction to statistical quality control (SQC).
uos: 1.a. Appreciate importance of industrial engineering, productivity and work study.
1.b. Describe ways to enhance productivity for given simple cases.
1.c. Explain concept and importance of SQC

units.title: Work Study.
topics: 2.1. Work study-Definition, techniques and role to enhance productivity.
2.2. Importance of human factors in application of work study techniques.
2.3. Basic procedure of method study.
2.4. Methods of recording data for method study using standard symbols, process charts and diagrams.
2.5. Preparation of operation (outline) process chart for given mechanical assembly having 6-8 components.
2.6. Process planning-concept, meaning, importance, functions, procedure and forms used.
2.7. Information required for process planning and information available from process planning.
2.8. Prepare process plan for given mechanical components, take 2-3 components.
2.9. Preparation of flow process chart and flow diagram for given mechanical components having at least 6-8 major operations.

2.10. Given the process plan, operation process chart and flow diagram, develop questioning techniques in analyzing data for method study. Also develop and improve the method, based on analysis of given data.

2.11. Principles of motion economy Industrial Engineering Course Code: 3351904 GTU/ NITTTR Bhopal/14-15 Gujarat State 3 applied in (a) use of human body, (b) design of work place layout (c) design of tools and equipment.
2.12. Principles of micro motion study, Therbligs and SIMO chart.
2.13. Man and machine chart.
2.14. Basic procedure of work measurement.
2.15. Equipment used in time study.
2.16. Job elements and their types.
2.17. Methods of measuring time- cumulative and fly back timing.
2.18. Concept of rating and rating scale.
2.19. Allowances-types, normal values and applications.
2.20. Calculation of basic time, standard time and work content.
2.21. Concept of work sampling/ activity sampling.
uos: 2.a. Define work study, method study and work measurement.
2.b. State the basic procedure of work study, method study and work measurement.
2.c. Prepare in the standard formats the outline process chart, flow process chart, flow diagrams, man machine chart and process plan for given data.
2.d. Modify given process plan and flow diagram for improvements.
2.e. State principles of motion economy.
2.f. Analyze work content and calculate standard time in a given situation.

units.title: Quality Assurance.
topics: 3.1. Definition of quality, quality control (QC), quality assurance (QA), statistical quality control (SQC) and reliability.
3.2. Importance of quality.
3.3. Difference between reliability and quality control.
3.4. Factors affecting and improving reliability.
3.5. QA tools.
3.6. Concept of total quality cycle, quality of design, quality of performance, quality of conformity and total quality.
3.7. Difference between inspection and quality control.
3.8. Fundamentals of statistics-types of variations, frequency, class boundary and midpoint, frequency distribution, frequency histogram, frequency bar chart and polygon chart.
3.9. Frequency distribution curve, central tendency, spread or dispersion and range, mode, median and mean, standard deviation and variance with numeric examples.
3.10. Concept of probability and normal distribution.
3.11. Area under normal distribution and examples on normal distribution.
3.12. Introduction to binomial and Poisson distribution. Industrial Engineering Course Code: 3351904 GTU/ NITTTR Bhopal/14-15 Gujarat State 4
uos: 3.a. Appreciate importance of quality.
3.b. Define quality, quality control (QC), quality assurance (QA), statistical quality control (SQC) and reliability
3.c. Differentiate between inspection and quality control.
3.d. Calculate mean, mode, median and standard deviation for simple data.
3.e. Prepare suitable frequency distribution chart for a given data.
3.f. Determine central tendency and dispersion in a given situation.
3.g. Calculate probabilities using normal distribution.
3.h. Define binomial and Poisson distribution.

units.title: Statistical Quality Control (SQC).
topics: 4.1. Concept of variability.
4.2. SQC tools and statistical fundamentals.
4.3. Concept and differences between variables and attributes.
4.4. Control charts for variable quality- types, objectives, applications, calculations of control limits and range/mean, methods to plot and interpretations (X bar-R chart) and examples.
4.5. Control charts for attribute quality- types, objectives, applications, calculations of control limits and range/mean, methods to plot and interpretations (p, np, 100p and c chart) and examples.
4.6. Process capability – meaning, definition and method to calculate, numeric examples.

4.7. Acceptance sampling: i. Quality control of incoming raw material and components. ii. Concepts of random sampling. iii. Sampling plans: definition, terminology, types (Single, double and multiple), implementing plans based on given input. iv. OC curve-concept, need, types and importance, interpretation of given OC curve.
uos: 4.a. Explain various tools of SQC.
4.b. Compare variables and attributes
4.c. Calculate control limits, range / mean and prepare control charts.
4.d. Calculate number/ percentage of items falling in and outside specifications limits from mean and standard deviation using normal distribution curve.
4.e. State and explain various methods of acceptance of incoming materials
4.f. Prepare and operate single and double sampling plans on the basis of given lot size, AQL and inspection level.
4.g. Describe process capability.
4.h. Explain consumers and producers risk.
4.i. State the importance of OC curve and interpret OC curves in a given situation.

units.title: Plant layout and material handling equipments.
topics: 5.1. Plant layout: Definition and concept.
5.2. Types of plant layout, their applications, advantages and limitations.
5.3. Role of material handling systems in industries.
5.4. Material handling equipment- Classification, types, specifications, applications and selection criteria.
uos: 5.a. Explain various types of plant layouts with their merits, demerits and their application.
5.b. Describe importance and applications of material handling equipment.
5.c. Select material handling equipments for given situation.

topics: 6.1. International Organization for standardization and its role, ISO standard series and quality managements system.

uos: 6.a. Explain ISO and its role in industries and business.
6.b. Explain TQC and TQM and its applications.
